title: Topic 1: Travel Plans
content:
1. Where are you planning to travel next, and why did you choose that destination?
2. How do you usually prepare before going on a trip?
3. Do you prefer travelling with a tour group or planning the trip yourself? Why?

questions.answer: I am planning to travel to Da Nang, a beautiful coastal city in central Vietnam, during my next summer break.
questions.example: I plan to go there with my family for four days in July to go swimming and visit the old town nearby.
questions.q: 1. Where are you planning to travel next, and why did you choose that destination?
questions.reason: I chose it simply because it offers breathtaking beaches, delicious local food, and a chance to relax my mind and broaden my knowledge of local culture.

questions.answer: Before a trip, I always check the weather forecast, book tickets early, and make a simple checklist of things to pack.
questions.example: Last time I went to Da Lat, I booked our homestay two weeks in advance and packed warm jackets.
questions.q: 2. How do you usually prepare before going on a trip?
questions.reason: Preparing carefully helps me stay on the safe side, fit everything comfortably within my budget, and avoid unnecessary stress during the holiday.

questions.answer: I prefer planning the trip myself with my family or friends rather than joining a big tour group.
questions.example: When we travel on our own, we can spend extra time at our favorite coffee shop or beach without rushing.
questions.q: 3. Do you prefer travelling with a tour group or planning the trip yourself? Why?
questions.reason: Self-planned trips give us more personal privacy and flexible schedules so our minds can slow down, relax comfortably, and enjoy quality time together.

3. What can schools or families do to encourage children to recycle more?
title: Topic 2: Recycling Habits
content:
1. Do you frequently use recycled products or separate household recyclable waste?
2. Are recycling programs and environmental awareness common among people in your neighborhood?
3. What can schools or families do to encourage children to recycle more?

questions.answer: Yes, I try to separate plastic bottles and paper at home and reuse cloth bags whenever I go shopping.
questions.example: For example, my family keeps two separate bins in the kitchen and sells old cardboard boxes and plastic bottles for recycling every month.
questions.q: 1. Do you frequently use recycled products or separate household recyclable waste?
questions.reason: Doing small green habits every day helps me make a contribution to protecting the environment and reducing plastic waste.

questions.answer: Environmental awareness is becoming more common in my neighborhood, though recycling programs still need to improve.
questions.example: Last Sunday morning, our local youth group organized a neighborhood clean-up and put new recycling bins along the main street.
questions.q: 2. Are recycling programs and environmental awareness common among people in your neighborhood?
questions.reason: Many young people now choose reusable cups and join clean-up days, but some busy residents still throw all their trash into one bag.

questions.answer: Parents and schools can set a good example every day and organize fun recycling activities for children.
questions.example: For instance, primary schools can hold small contests where kids exchange old paper or plastic bottles for green plants or notebooks.
questions.q: 3. What can schools or families do to encourage children to recycle more?
questions.reason: When children raise their awareness and choose green habits early, they learn important values and actively get involved in environmental protection as they grow up.

- Pursuing a career as a wellness and life coach (huấn luyện viên phong cách sống và sức khỏe toàn diện)
Which option do you think is the best choice and why?
title: Part 2 - Situation 1: Advising a Helper-Minded Friend on a Health & Wellness Career
content:
Situation: Your close friend has a genuine passion for helping people lead healthier lives and wants to transition into the wellness field. He is considering three career paths:
- Becoming a personal fitness trainer (huấn luyện viên thể hình cá nhân)
- Working as a certified nutritionist (chuyên gia tư vấn dinh dưỡng)
- Pursuing a career as a wellness and life coach (huấn luyện viên phong cách sống và sức khỏe toàn diện)
Which option do you think is the best choice and why?

chosen.khen1Text: because he can work at a fitness center close to home, which saves daily travel time, and the training courses to become a personal trainer are easy for him to afford.

khen2ARE.answer: This career brings both my friend and his clients a wide range of benefits because it is directly beneficial to physical health.
khen2ARE.example: For instance, he can guide busy office workers through simple 45-minute gym workouts after work so they feel more energetic and avoid back pain.
khen2ARE.reason: To be more specific, working as a fitness trainer allows him to stay active every day while helping others keep fit, get into good shape, and raise public awareness of a healthy lifestyle and diseases.

chosen.khen3Text: a safe and practical job to gain real working experience, build confidence, and get ready for a stable career in the fitness field.

rejected.reason: becoming a certified nutritionist requires years of difficult medical study and high tuition fees, which creates financial worry when my friend wants to switch careers soon.

rejected.option: Pursuing a career as a wellness and life coach
rejected.reason: the job of a life coach is still unclear to many local people, so finding paying clients is hard, and this opinion has received little agreement in similar career situations.

reusedVocab: close to home, which saves daily travel time
raise public awareness of healthy lifestyle and diseases
gain real working experience, build confidence, and get ready for a stable career

He is considering three career paths: becoming a personal fitness trainer, working as a certified nutritionist, or pursuing a career as a wellness and life coach.

title: Part 3 - Topic 1: The Role of Extracurricular Activities for Children
content:
Topic: The positive contributions of extracurricular activities to children's growth
Suggestions:
- Cultivating a balanced lifestyle between study and leisure
- Developing essential time management skills
- Enhancing social communication and teamwork abilities
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. What extracurricular activities would you recommend for primary school pupils?
2. How can parents help their children balance formal schoolwork with extracurricular commitments?
3. Should universities consider extracurricular participation as a mandatory criterion for student admission?

hint.coreTopic: the positive role of extracurricular activities for children

followUps.answer: There are some great activities for primary school children, such as swimming, drawing, and learning a musical instrument.
followUps.example: For example, practicing music for thirty minutes after school helps young kids relax and improve their memory.
followUps.formula: What -> There are some [Ns], such as...
followUps.q: What extracurricular activities would you recommend for primary school pupils?
followUps.reason: This is because swimming improves physical fitness, while learning guitar or drawing allows their brain to exercise creatively.

followUps.answer: I think parents should help their children create a simple daily timetable and avoid joining too many clubs at once.
followUps.example: For instance, parents can let their child join just one sport club on weekends while keeping weekday evenings for homework and rest.
followUps.q: How can parents help their children balance formal schoolwork with extracurricular commitments?
followUps.reason: Breaking tasks into small daily steps helps children finish homework on time without feeling stressed or tired.

followUps.answer: No, I don't think universities should make after-school clubs a strict requirement for every student.
followUps.example: For example, a hardworking rural student with high exam scores might miss out on university if clubs were required.
followUps.q: Should universities consider extracurricular participation as a mandatory criterion for student admission?
followUps.reason: This is because some students from poor families must work part-time or help with housework, so they do not have free time or money for extra clubs.

mindmapPoints.cue: Cultivating a balanced lifestyle between study and leisure
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because playing sports or music after school allows children to unwind, relieve stress, and stay away from boring screen time.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for both their physical health and mental health.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Extracurricular activities help children keep a healthy balance between study and free time.

mindmapPoints.expand: For example, a student in a football club learns to finish school homework early so they can attend practice on time.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to children's daily habits and school discipline.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Joining after-school clubs helps children learn important time management skills.

mindmapPoints.cue: Enhancing social communication and teamwork abilities
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because joining clubs lets children meet like-minded friends, share common interests, and build a strong sense of belonging through face-to-face interaction.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on their social network and confidence.
mindmapPoints.sentence: After-school activities help children improve communication and teamwork skills.

hint.ownIdea: I think that 3 ideas are comprehensive. I cannot think of other ideas.
reusedVocab: build a strong sense of belonging
